To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
high-redshift Herschel starbursts are metal-rich and extremely obscured in Hα.

high-redshift starburst galaxies, selected from Herschel observations, have on average a metallicity similar to that of main-sequence galaxies of similar stellar masses and red-shifts, and an extremely obscured star formation component, which is optically thin even in Hα, and that is responsible for ~90% of their total SFR.

(i) the starburst galaxies are metal-rich outliers from MS galaxies at the same stellar mass and redshift; (ii) the optical spectra are dominated by the contribution from an optically thick component that contains ~90% of the total star formation rate; (iii) the optical spectra show evidence of a high electron density, which is consistent with a major merger scenario.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physical properties of the starburst galaxies at high redshift.
the study of high-redshift starburst galaxies, which are analogues of local ULIRG galaxies.
the physical properties of the starburst galaxies at z ~ 1-2 and their relation to the local starburst population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
high-redshift starburst galaxies, like their local counterparts, are a mixture of optically thin and thick regions.

high-redshift MS outliers are analogs to local ULIRGs, but we cannot rule out the possibility that they are also analogs to local starburst-dominated LIRGs, which have a lower fraction of obscured SFR.
the high-redshift starburst galaxies are similar to the local ULIRGs, but with higher SFR and metallicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
high-z MS starburst galaxies are similar to local ULIRGs, but with lower metallicity and higher electron density.
high-redshift MS outliers have properties that are similar to the local ULIRG population, but with a higher metal content.
high-z MS galaxies are not only more metal-poor than their lower-redshift counterparts but also have a more metal-poor circumnuclear region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optical spectrum of a galaxy with a strong starburst is not a good tracer of its total SFR.
the starburst phase in high-redshift galaxies is characterized by a very high level of dust obscuration, with only a minor contribution from optically unobscured regions.

Herschel and optical spectra are both necessary to characterize the properties of high-z MS outliers, and that the optical spectra can reveal important information about the physical conditions of the starburst regions.
